data.body:
Gerrit 1630 first pass: **Verified +1** (CI green, run 31565338683) but **LLM-Review -1** on a single blocking finding — `bugfix-size-attestation`: the change touches 167 non-test lines, over the 150-line floor for a ticket typed **bug**, and this ticket carried no plan-review attestation. Per docs/plan-review-gate.md that criterion's remedy is a ticket action, not a code change (a large fix under a bug label should have a reviewed plan), so the diff was NOT shrunk to duck it.

Remediation: ran `rebar review-plan`. First run BLOCKed on one deterministic readiness item (P1 readiness-shape) — my heading read '## Acceptance criteria (the approved subset)' and the floor requires the exact `## Acceptance Criteria` heading. Renamed the heading, kept the ACs verbatim, re-ran: **PASS, signed**. `review-plan --status` now reports verdict=certified, currency_basis=file_impact, verified_at_sha=94abd87ab0827293fc0a0ba2adba9e98a0c2d7c3. No description edits after signing, so it will not go stale-material.

The review left one advisory (E4): it read the plan's note that the tally is fed 'from the JSON Check 1 ALREADY parses' and objected that fsck.py:100 discards its `json.load(f)` result. That is accurate about the code as it stood — and is precisely what the patch changes: Check 1 now binds that parse as `env_authorship.observe(filename, json.load(f))`. The plan described the post-change state; no extra I/O pass is introduced. Non-blocking, no action needed.

Posted `rerun-llm-review` on 1630; Verified should re-run on the same patchset. No code changed for this remediation, so no amend was needed.
